summary.title: Using convolutional neural nets to detect facial keypoints tutorial
summary.one_liner: You learn to build and improve neural nets for the Kaggle Facial Keypoint Detection challenge using Lasagne and Theano, progressing from a dense net to convolutional nets with data augmentation and learning-rate/momentum schedules.
keywords: how to detect face landmarks with neural nets
takeaways: Convolutional layers (local connectivity, weight sharing, pooling) reduce parameters and improve results over a fully connected net on 96x96 face images.
Horizontal-flip data augmentation requires flipping the x-coordinates of targets and swapping left/right keypoint columns via a flip_indices list.
Training data can be augmented on the fly in a custom BatchIterator, at little extra cost, rather than doubling the stored dataset.
Decreasing the learning rate and increasing momentum over epochs (via on_epoch_finished callbacks and Theano shared variables) speeds up training.
summary.summary: The tutorial walks through the Kaggle Facial Keypoint Detection challenge, with setup via Lasagne, Theano and nolearn on a CUDA GPU. It starts with a simple fully connected net on flattened images, then builds a LeNet5-style convolutional net with three conv/max-pool stages and two dense layers, comparing learning curves and RMSE. Later sections add horizontal-flip data augmentation with a custom batch iterator and a learning-rate and momentum schedule to shorten training. The page is the first part of a series; the text ends partway through the learning-rate section.
